'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Minister of Defence (Sweden)|Swedish Defence Minister]] [[Pål Jonson]] announces that [[Sweden]] [[List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War|will send]] its self-propelled [[Archer Artillery System]], 50 [[Combat Vehicle 90]] [[Infantry fighting vehicle|IFVs]], and [[NLAW]] [[anti-tank warfare|anti-tank missiles]] to [[Ukraine]] as part of its latest military support package for the [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian military]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/sweden-to-send-archer-artillery-to-ukraine-war-russia/ (Politico)]
*[[Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso]]
**Sixteen [[Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland|VDP]] members and 14 civilians are killed during four attacks by [[Islamic extremism|Islamic extremists]] in [[Burkina Faso]]. At least ten attackers are also killed. [https://www.voanews.com/a/attacks-kill-dozens-in-burkina-faso-security-sources-say-/6927428.html (VOA)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**A [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] teacher and a member of the [[Jenin Brigades]] are killed, and three others are injured, in a raid by [[Israeli Defense Forces|Israeli soldiers]] at a [[refugee camp]] in [[Jenin]], in the [[West Bank]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/1/19/teacher-among-two-palestinians-killed-by-israeli-forces-in-jenin (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-64330051 (BBC News)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**Three [[Law enforcement in Pakistan|police officers]] are killed in a [[Suicide attack|suicide bombing]] at a police outpost in [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/pakistani-taliban-attacks-police-outpost-killing-three-officers-2023-01-19/ (Reuters)]
*Five [[Iraqis]] from [[Duhok]], [[Kurdistan Region]], [[Iraq]], are shot and killed by gunmen on a road in [[Mardin Province]], [[Turkey]]. Two of the victims were prominent [[imam]]s in Duhok. [https://www.thenationalnews.com/mena/2023/01/19/four-iraqis-killed-in-shooting-in-turkey/ (''The National News'')]
 
'''Business and economy'''
*[[2023 United States debt-ceiling crisis]]
**The [[United States]] reaches its [[United States debt ceiling|debt ceiling]] of $31.4 trillion, requiring the [[United States Department of the Treasury|Treasury Department]] to suspend the issuance of new [[United States Treasury security|Treasury securities]] and take [[United States debt ceiling#Extraordinary measures|extraordinary measures]] to prevent a default. [https://www.cnn.com/2023/01/19/politics/debt-ceiling-deadline-treasury/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Retail apocalypse]]
**[[United Kingdom|British]] [[catalog merchant|catalog retailer]] [[Argos (retailer)|Argos]] says that it will close all of its stores in the [[Republic of Ireland]] by June, with the loss of 580 jobs, saying that the investment needed to modernize its operations in the country was "not viable". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cj7287r24vjo (BBC News)]
*[[Netflix]] co-founder [[Reed Hastings]] steps down as co-CEO, having served in the position since its founding in 1997. [[Greg Peters (businessman)|Greg Peters]] is selected to succeed him. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-64337098 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Basra International Stadium stampede]]
**One person is killed and around 60 others are injured during a [[Crowd collapses and crushes|stampede]] at a stadium in [[Basra]], [[Iraq]]. It is suspected that the incident occurred when some people tried to push their way into the stadium. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-64330050.amp (BBC)]
*Fifteen [[Armenian Armed Forces|servicemen]] are killed and seven others are injured in a fire at a [[barracks]] in [[Azat, Armenia|Azat]], [[Armenia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/politics-armenia-azerbaijan-fires-19dc0b8d63fa328620d95e5548d52b43 (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Iran–South Korea relations]]
**[[Iran]] and [[South Korea]] summon each other's [[ambassador]]s in a deepening dispute between the countries, after [[South Korean President]] [[Yoon Suk-yeol]] called Iran "the enemy of the [[United Arab Emirates]]" while addressing [[Republic of Korea Army|South Korean troops]] stationed there. [https://www.reuters.com/world/south-korea-envoy-iran-summoned-over-yoons-enemy-remarks-media-2023-01-19/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2022–2023 Peruvian political protests]]
**Thousands of protesters march in [[Lima]] demanding the [[resignation]] of [[President of Peru|president]] [[Dina Boluarte]] as the number of deaths from clashes between [[political demonstration|demonstrators]] and police exceeds 50. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peru-protesters-fired-up-by-deaths-march-lima-demanding-change-2023-01-19/ (Reuters)]
*A judge in [[Bolivia]] rules that opposition figure [[Luis Fernando Camacho]] must remain in prison ahead of his trial. Camacho was arrested in December on charges of [[terrorism]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/bolivia-judge-rules-opposition-governor-remain-pre-trial-detention-2023-01-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[President of Sierra Leone|Sierra Leonean president]] [[Julius Maada Bio]] signs into law a [[gender equality]] bill mandating the employment of at least 30 percent of [[Women in Sierra Leone|women]] across all businesses. The law also guarantees at least 14 weeks of [[maternity leave]] and [[equal pay]]. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/overseas/01/20/23/sierra-leone-passes-law-reserving-30-of-jobs-for-women (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Protests against Emmanuel Macron]]
**[[2023 French pension reform strikes]]
***A day of strikes and demonstrations occurs throughout [[France]] against the [[Borne government|government]]'s pension reform project, which proposes to raise the [[retirement age]] to 64. [https://www.lepoint.fr/societe/en-direct-greve-du-19-janvier-une-journee-de-perturbations-et-de-manifestations-19-01-2023-2505389_23.php (''Le Point'')]
*[[2023 Kazakh legislative election]]
**[[President of Kazakhstan|President]] [[Kassym-Jomart Tokayev]] [[Dissolution of parliament|dissolves]] the [[Mäjilis]], ending the [[7th Parliament of Kazakhstan|seventh convocation]], and calls for a [[snap election]] on March 19. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/kazakh-leader-dissolves-parliament-calls-march-election/article66408960.ece (AFP via ''The Hindu'')]
*[[Resignation of Jacinda Ardern]]
**[[Jacinda Ardern]] announces her intention to resign as [[prime minister of New Zealand]] no later than February 7. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/jan/19/jacinda-ardern-resigns-as-prime-minister-of-new-zealand (''The Guardian'')]
